title: "They want to rule over men" - Jason Whitlock doubles down on Stephen Jackson blasting WNBA announcers over A'ja Wilson - NewsBreak
text:
By Bruno Feliks ,
4 hours ago
The Indiana Fever and Las Vegas Aces are gearing up for Game 3 of a phenomenal playoff series that has already delivered two sensational matchups between the two currently best basketball players in the world. In Game 1, A’ja Wilson showcased the full mastery of her game with 38 points and 16 rebounds, only for Caitlin Clark to answer right back in Game 2 with 27 points and 15 assists.
However, in a series that also features star players like Kelsey Mitchell, Jackie Young, Chelsea Gray, Aliyah Boston and even Sophie Cunningham, who generates media interest all on her own, everything boiled down to Wilson’s interaction with a male fan in Game 2.
Whitlock isn’t holding back on Wilson The four-time MVP took a lot of heat for her emotional outburst, for which the WNBA ultimately did not suspend her.
Among the fiercest reactions was the one of Stephen Jackson, who called out WNBA announcers for not holding her accountable , a sentiment immediately backed by Jason Whitlock .
“Absolutely LOVE it. Glad to hear Stack say this. He and Ron Artest had their careers severely damaged over the Malice in the Palace,” Whitlock posted on his “X” account. “Hope these dudes are waking up that these women don’t want equality. They want to rule over men. Wow. Thank you, Stack.”
Stephen A. as an example Jackson brought up Stephen A. Smith as an example, pointing out that while he doesn’t agree with him on everything, Smith gave them their flowers when they deserved it and criticized them when they earned it.
The former NBA champ with the San Antonio Spurs then warned all WNBA members that they must be careful when demanding equality with the NBA, because when the time comes to take a lot of media heat, they have to be ready for it.
Related: “They didn’t want to give him his money” – Tim Hardaway urges Jalen Duren not to settle for Detroit’s $200 million offer
Mounting media pressure Still, anyone who expected the reigning Finals MVP and WNBA champion to be suspended ahead of a potential game of the season, one expected to shatter all viewership records, is either new to the game or simply naive.
You don’t have to look far back in history; it’s enough to remember Victor Wembanyama’s elbow to Naz Reid’s throat earlier this year. The league decided to protect one of its biggest stars, and that is clearly a practice the WNBA is sticking to as well.
Either way, with such explosive growth in popularity, Wilson and other WNBA players will soon have to get used to mounting media pressure surrounding incidents like this.
Related: New camera angle proves that A’ja Wilson overreacted when she attacked the Fever fan
